name: Arleigh Burke Flight IIA destroyer
role: Aegis guided-missile destroyer with twin helicopter hangars for air defence, surface warfare, anti-submarine warfare and land strike

serviceWindow.statusNotes: The date is that of the example ship, USS Mustin (DDG 89), commissioned on 26 July 2003. Flight IIA ships are in active service as of 2026-03-15 and make up the largest group of Arleigh Burke hulls.

dimensions.crew: about 380 officers and enlisted (USS Mustin figure)

propulsionSummary: Four General Electric LM2500-30 gas turbines drive two shafts for about 100,000 shaft horsepower.

weapons.name: RIM-66M SM-2MR
weapons.mountSummary: Fired from the 96-cell Mk 41 vertical launch system, shared with ESSM, Tomahawk and ASROC. Quantity is a typical mix, not a published load. The Navy fact file gives SM-2 Medium Range as up to 90 nautical miles (about 167 km), so the 93 km engine range is estimated. ESSM, which a real Flight IIA also carries, is not modelled in this row set.

weapons.name: RGM-84 Harpoon
weapons.mountSummary: Two quad launchers on early Flight IIA ships. Many newer hulls do not carry them. The Navy fact file gives Harpoon range as over 67 nautical miles (about 124 km), so the 139 km engine range is estimated.

weapons.name: Mk 15 Phalanx CIWS
weapons.mountSummary: 20 mm six-barrel gun. Fitted to some Flight IIA ships, not all. FAS lists Phalanx range as classified, so range and round count are estimated.

sensors.name: AN/SPY-1D(V) phased-array radar
sensors.role: Aegis air search and track with the (V) littoral upgrade for clutter near land, four fixed arrays on the deckhouse

sensors.name: AN/SPS-67(V)3 surface search radar
sensors.role: Surface search and navigation, picks out ships and low flyers

sensors.name: AN/SPG-62 fire control radars (3)
sensors.role: Illuminates the target for semi-active SM-2 missiles in the last seconds of flight

sensors.name: AN/SQS-53C bow sonar
sensors.role: Hull-mounted active and passive search for submarines

sensors.name: AN/SQR-19 towed array
sensors.role: Passive long-range listening for submarines on a cable towed behind the ship

sensors.name: AN/SLQ-32(V)3 electronic support
sensors.role: Detects, identifies and bears on hostile radars

sensors.name: Bridge and lookout watch
sensors.role: Eyes and binoculars from the bridge and weather decks

radar.note: Hull shaping from the DDG 51 design, with twin hangars adding structure aft. Still a 155 m steel ship.

infrared.note: Four gas turbines put out a strong exhaust plume, so the ship shows up clearly to heat-seeking sensors at close range.

acoustic.note: Gas turbine ships are louder than diesel-electric types, and the towed array and bow sonar make her an active participant in the underwater fight.

visual.note: A 154 m grey hull with a tall deckhouse is easy to see on a clear day, but it shows a low profile from a distance.

brief.whatItIs: The Flight IIA is the most common version of the Arleigh Burke destroyer. It adds two helicopter hangars at the stern, so the ship carries its own helicopters instead of only landing them. The SPY-1D(V) radar and Aegis combat system are the same family as Flight II. USS Mustin (DDG 89) is the example ship.
brief.howItIsUsed: A commander uses it the same way as a Flight II: as an air-defence escort that stays on the threat side of the carrier or convoy with the SPY-1D(V) radar on. The hangars change the picture below the surface and over the horizon. Two MH-60R helicopters give it a second set of eyes against submarines and small boats, and they can carry anti-submarine torpedoes and Hellfire missiles. Standard missiles handle aircraft and missiles at long range, ESSM adds close-in air defence, and Tomahawk gives land strike. The weakness is the same as any destroyer: the vertical launch cells are the magazine and cannot be reloaded quickly at sea. Treat the missile counts in this record as typical, not fixed.
typicalMissions: Air and missile defence of a carrier or convoy
